messages.subject: Residual Shape Component
parts:
Dear geomorph users,

I have a mainly theoretical question related to the RSC/CAC graphical output resulting from procD.allometry in geomorph. According to Mitteroecker et al. (2004) the Common Allometric Component is estimated from "the common allometry estimated by a pooled regression of the shape variables, corrected for their species means, on size". The first residual shape component, plotted against the CAC is used in the same paper to visualize species shape along the CAC component. I tried out this approach in geomorph:

mult_reg <- procD.allometry(shape~size, logsz = TRUE, data=gdfALLOMETRY, iter=9999, print.progress = FALSE)
plot(mult_reg, method = "CAC")



 RSC1 vs CAC graph shows an overlap between species. Given that RSC1 represents the principal compoenent of the residuals of shape coordinates after size is regressed out, I would assume that this means that all differences between my different species (different colors) is explained by size. However, this is not the case, as size explains only 16% of the shape differences:

Homogeneity of Slopes Test
                  ResDf     RSS       SS       MS      Rsq      F      Z     P Pr(>F)
Common Allometry    233 0.74071                                                      
Group Allometries   227 0.71512 0.025596 0.004266 0.012765 1.3541 12.878 1e-04       
Total               240 2.00522                                                   240

The null hypothesis of parallel slopes is rejected
  based on a significance criterion of alpha = 0.05 

Based on the results of this test, the following ANOVA table is most appropriate

Type I (Sequential) Sums of Squares and Cross-products
Randomized Residual Permutation Procedure Used
10000 Permutations
ANOVA effect sizes and P-values based on empirical F distributions


              Df      SS      MS     Rsq        F      Z Pr(>F)    
log(size)      1 0.32634 0.32634 0.16275 103.5915 10.029  1e-04 ***
gp             6 0.93816 0.15636 0.46786  49.6332 20.880  1e-04 ***
log(size):gp   6 0.02560 0.00427 0.01276   1.3541 12.878  1e-04 ***
Residuals    227 0.71512 0.00315 0.35663                           
Total        240 2.00522                                           
---
Signif. codes:  0 ‘***’ 0.001 ‘**’ 0.01 ‘*’ 0.05 ‘.’ 0.1 ‘ ’ 1

Am I interpreting this output correctly? Or does geomorph consider these terms (RSC and CAC) differently from Mitteroecker et al. (2004)?

Thank you in advance for your help.


Best regards,
Sérgio.

messages.author: 511e44c7d1e1bab0
messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] Residual Shape Component
parts:
Sergio,

I can only comment on some of the points you raised, as I cannot see the plot you attached, but I think it is worth considering the following:

- geomorph implements CAC and RSC exactly as proposed by Mitteroecker et al 2004

- "Given that RSC1 represents the principal component of the residuals of shape coordinates after size is regressed out..." notice that this is not exactly accurate, as to calculate CAC one first mean-centers each group. In this sense, then, only the part of shape variation associated to size that is COMMON to all groups is captured by CAC, and RSC is "residual" only in respect to that part of shape variation.

- In your case, it seems like assuming a common allometry, as is done under the CAC, might not be optimal. This is evident in your test for homogeneity of slopes, where the significant interaction between of CS and group suggests different groups have different allometric trajectories. This would make me consider to what extent you actually want to be looking at CAC, which is calculated under a single slope. It might be more useful to look at Regression Scores and Predicted lines to see how shape covaries with size across groups, or perform a pairwise comparison of slopes.

Finally, just as a side comment, note that procD.allometry has been deprecated in the most recent version of geomorph, released last week. To see how you can implement the same kind of analyses using the new functions, please see the vignette that is now included in the new version.

Hope this helps

Antigoni

messages.author: 4d71c6e24fb21497
messages.subject: RE: [geomorph-r-package] Residual Shape Component
parts:
To add and reconfirm,

 

Yes, geomorph calculates the CAC and RSC exactly as proposed in Mitteroecker et al. 2004. It is their method implemented in R.

 

As to this dataset, please look at your anova table again. Nearly half of your variation is explained by group differences, and explains considerably more variation than does the common (or separate) allometry. In fact, the plot of size vs CAC shows this: species trajectories are parallel, but more distinct.

 

As for CAC vs. RSC1, it is not intuitive to predict whether groups should, or should not be, distinct in this plot. That requires considerable allometry in terms of strength of signal (again relative to groups).

 

Unfortunately, Mitteroecker et al. 2004 did not provide their anova tables to explain how such effects relate to the patterns observed across the two plots; obfuscating understanding of their approach and what is expected in these plots.

 

Best,


Dean
